title: Newcastle told they must up offer for Atlanta United’s Miguel Almirón
trail: Newcastle have been told that they must improve their offer for Miguel Almirón if they want to sign him from Atlanta United this month
body: Newcastle have been told that they must improve their offer for Miguel Almirón if they want to sign him from Atlanta United this month. The Paraguay playmaker’s agent has confirmed he has held talks with Newcastle about a potential move, with personal terms understood to have already been agreed. However, with owner Mike Ashley having yet to make progress in his attempts to sell the club, Newcastle have yet to submit an offer anywhere near Atlanta’s valuation of £30m and the 24-year-old’s representative is adamant he will not be allowed to leave unless they increase their bid. “There are two to three clubs in England that have interest in him, but we haven’t advanced a lot yet,” Daniel Campos told the Paraguayan radio station ABC Cardinal. “If Newcastle raise their offers, they could be one of the clubs, but there are other clubs. There are clubs from England, Germany, Italy and Spain that are interested in Miguel Almirón, but we aren’t going to rush things. “With Newcastle, I spoke about the player’s salary, but the club needs to raise their offers with Atlanta if they want to get the player. Miguel Almirón’s value is high, it’s not for any club to sign him.” Reports on Tyneside on Monday suggested that Newcastle had pulled out of the race to sign him due to “astronomical” wage demands of £100,000 a week but that is not understood to be the case. Rafael Benítez has identified Almirón as his preferred transfer target as Newcastle bid for Premier League survival. Meanwhile, Ayoze Pérez has admitted there is something “wrong” at Newcastle as they prepare to face Chelsea on Saturday at Stamford Bridge. They have won only just four times in all competitions this season, a run which culminated in Saturday’s 1-1 FA Cup third round draw with Blackburn at St James’ Park. Asked about that game, Pérez said: “Something is wrong. It wasn’t good enough, but we have to keep going now. It’s going to be a long January but we must stick together and face up to it.” Asked to elaborate, the 25-year-old Spaniard added: “I don’t know exactly, but it is a strange thing. You can’t struggle as much as we are in home games. That means something is wrong. It is strange because there is no consistency. Sometimes it is individual performances, sometimes it’s not like that and it’s team performance. “It can’t be individual every time as we have changed players and rotated. I think there is a piece of the jigsaw that is missing. It is holding us back and it’s why we are struggling. We’ve won twice at home and that’s just not acceptable. It’s not good enough so something should change.”
